Decision ballot · goal-run inbox-v2-revamp-2026-08-01

Which direction becomes the inbox

Three candidates went through tournament, three judge seats scored them independently, the panel arbitrated a winner plus grafts. This run does not converge on your behalf. Read the verdict block below, then reply in chat with your pick. Two minutes is enough.

Seat1st2nd3rd
Ergonomics (taps, wrong-action risk)v2bv2cv2a
Craft (native-ness, desktop composition)v2cv2bv2a
IA scalability (growth cost, coherence)v2cv2bv2a
Winner: v2c "workbench." It takes craft and IA outright, places second on ergonomics, and is the only candidate that answers the audit's central desktop finding structurally (rail + working list + a real Claude peer instead of a placeholder) rather than cosmetically. v2b places second on every seat and donates the largest graft list, including the one DB-level fix (U1) neither other candidate touched. v2a places third on all three seats: safest, cleanest code, moves the fewest ergonomics needles, but keeps the tournament's best chat internals, which v2c grafts wholesale. Not a landslide, all three ship for reference regardless, the final call is yours.

01

Rendered evidence: before vs after

The audit's central desktop finding: Inbox spent roughly two-thirds of a 1440px canvas on a glyph and the words "Select a conversation." The winner's answer is structural: the default peer becomes Claude, not a placeholder.

BeforeToday · baseline, live production
AfterToday · v2c + v2b's cockpit masthead graft

Masthead is now a single number defined as the sum of its own zone counts (14 = 3 + 11 + 0), with a stacked bar of the same three counts, the summary cannot drift from its parts. The old inline "Approve & send" button, which acted on a cached brief, is gone; each pending item now names its one owning surface.

BeforeInbox · baseline, live production

Selecting no conversation leaves most of a 1440px canvas dead: a glyph and "Select a conversation."

AfterWorkbench · rail + list + thread peer + Claude peer

Four regions, all carrying content. The default peer is Claude, attached to what's on screen: the composer reads "Ask about <the item you're looking at>," and the surface admits in-copy that every Claude turn starts fresh (the broker never passes --resume).

BeforeToday · baseline, mobile 390px
AfterToday · v2c + grafts, mobile 390px

Same masthead-sum arithmetic and single-owner rows carry over unchanged to mobile.

02

More decisive crops

Ops at 1440px, fixed
All three tournament candidates shipped this broken or near-empty. The winner's build gives it a real state band, a freshness signal, and two columns when the region has the width.
Chat with tool cards and per-turn cost/latency
Grafted from v2a wholesale: tool-call cards, a cost-and-latency line on every turn, Hands-free as a labelled mode. Against the real broker, cost renders null (broker reports none) and only duration shows.
v2b, the runner-up's Home cockpit
Best single dashboard composition in the tournament; the only candidate with its own DB-level U1 guard. Sends and Ops render on the same screen, the 0-tap "is anything stuck" check that decided ergonomics.
v2a, chat-dock desktop
The best chat internals in the set, but the middle pane still reads "Select a conversation" while chat is compressed into a 440px dock, the softer version of the ghost-pane defect the winner solves outright.
v2b Home, mobile
Same cockpit zones, no tab-bar cost on either viewport.

Not purely additiveThe winner touches 16 shared production files

The DoD asked for default routes pixel-identical to the pre-run baseline. On the live site that still holds: nothing is deployed. But on the exp/v2 branch itself, applying the winner changes the default routes on purpose: the U1 send-safety guard, the missing fetch-failed states, the compose confirmation, and the doubled headers all live in shared production code, and fixing a send-safety landmine cannot also be invisible.

Ships unarmedClaude chat needs one command before it does anything

The broker (supabase/functions/inbox-claude) is already built, deployed and probed in production: auth, validation and CORS all verified correct. A real turn today returns "Claude is not armed yet: the container key is not set on the broker." because the upstream key isn't obtainable non-interactively. Arming is one command:

supabase secrets set RAILWAY_CLAUDE_API_KEY=<the API_KEY value from the Railway service>

On-device, by necessityVoice has no server leg

The Supabase vault has no OPENAI_API_KEY, so voice runs entirely on-device: webkitSpeechRecognition for input, speechSynthesis for output. That's a genuine upgrade for this app, not a fallback forced by a missing key: it removes two network legs from the reference's four-leg pipeline, costs nothing, needs no key. What it cannot prove: real dictation is unverified, because headless browsers expose the recognition constructor but cannot capture a live microphone. A human has to speak into it once on real Safari or Chrome.

Cleanup that still has to happen

Applying the winner is not the last step. The v2a and v2b branches (the losers of this ballot) and the stale #exp/c route both need deleting after the pick is made, none of that is done yet, on any branch.

05

Verified vs still open

Verified by instrument

Deploy fence holds. main unchanged at 7c9ea96, 0 commits pushed, no branch on the remote, winner sits on 20 unmerged commits on exp/v2.
Default-route probes. Today's masthead arithmetic holds on live data (4+12+0=16), zero approve buttons remain, Ops's doubled header is gone on the default route too, not just the gated surface.
Broker auth chain. No auth → 401, anon key → 401, Ivan's real JWT → reaches the upstream and correctly renders the unarmed state, 502 upstream_not_armed, oversized prompt → 413.
Secret grep clean. Zero leaked API keys, PATs or service-role JWTs in the built bundle or git history; the one JWT present is the intended public anon key.
Gate table. 44 shots, zero horizontal overflow, zero hard-clipped text, zero app console errors, three visibly distinct data states, no new npm dependency, zero monospace, severity stays 3-tier, build/lint/tests all clean (292 passing).
A live regression caught by the orchestrator's own probe, not the build. "Checked now ago", found and fixed with 4 new regression tests.

NOT verified: say-so, not a zero

A completed Claude turn. Requires RAILWAY_CLAUDE_API_KEY, which is not obtainable non-interactively. Everything up to the container's own auth check is proven; the leg past it is not.
Real dictation. Headless Chromium exposes the recognition constructor but cannot capture a microphone. Feature-detection is proven behaviourally; one human speaking into real Safari or Chrome is the only way to confirm the audio leg.
iOS PWA behaviour. Service worker plus microphone permission on an actual phone, untested.
Whether the revamp is actually better to live in. A week of real use answers that; no instrument does.
